# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/gendocs` from internal/config/vars.go and the settings definitions; do not edit. -->

awxnext is configured by environment variables, read when a process starts, and by settings,
kept in the database and changed through `/api/v2/settings/<category>/` (or the Settings pages)
by a system administrator, as in AWX.

## Environment variables

### Server

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AWXNEXT_DATABASE_URL` | `postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/awxnext?sslmode=disable` | PostgreSQL connection URL. |
| `AWXNEXT_LISTEN` | `:8052` | Address the API and UI listen on. |
| `AWXNEXT_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8052` | External URL: OIDC and SAML redirects, links in notifications. |
| `AWXNEXT_NODE_NAME` | the host name | This node's instance name; unique per node. |
| `AWXNEXT_INTERNAL_URL` |  | How the other control nodes reach this one, to forward a container group pod's or an agent's connection to the node running its job. |
| `AWXNEXT_SERVICE_URL` | `AWXNEXT_BASE_URL` | How container group job pods reach the control plane. |
| `AWXNEXT_UI_DIR` |  | Serve the web UI from this directory instead of the embedded build. |
| `AWXNEXT_METRICS_TOKEN` |  | Bearer token /metrics requires; open when empty. |
| `AWXNEXT_LOG_FORMAT` | `text` | text or json. |
| `AWXNEXT_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | debug, info, warn or error. |
| `AWXNEXT_DEV` |  | Development mode: an insecure default secret key, the database created when missing, websockets from UI dev servers on localhost. |

### Jobs

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AWXNEXT_PROJECTS_ROOT` | `/var/lib/awxnext/projects` | Project checkouts. |
| `AWXNEXT_JOBS_ROOT` | `/var/lib/awxnext/jobs` | Job working directories. |
| `AWXNEXT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` | `podman` | How jobs run on control nodes: podman or docker (in the execution environment's image), or none (ansible-runner on the PATH). |
| `AWXNEXT_RUNNER_CMD` | `ansible-runner` | ansible-runner for runtime none. |
| `AWXNEXT_JOB_ISOLATION` | `auto` | Runtime none: auto (each job as a job user of its own when awxnext-jobexec works, else as the server's user), users (required: the server does not start without) or off. |
| `AWXNEXT_JOB_EXEC` | `/usr/local/libexec/awxnext-jobexec` | The helper that runs a job as a job user (awxjob0, awxjob1, ...). |
| `AWXNEXT_DEFAULT_EE_IMAGE` | `quay.io/ansible/awx-ee:latest` | Image of the default execution environment created at the first start. |
| `AWXNEXT_CAPACITY` |  | Fixed forks capacity of this node, instead of the one its CPU and memory allow. |
| `AWXNEXT_SHIM_IMAGE` | `ghcr.io/damhau/awxnext:latest` | Image whose awxnext binary is copied into container group job pods. |
| `AWXNEXT_KEEP_JOB_PODS` |  | Keep container group job pods after their job (debugging). |
| `SYSTEM_TASK_FORKS_CPU` | `4` | Forks per CPU, as in AWX. |
| `SYSTEM_TASK_FORKS_MEM` | `100` | MB of memory per fork, as in AWX. |
| `SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_CPU` |  | Replaces a control node's measured CPUs (2, 1500m), as in AWX. |
| `SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_MEM` |  | Replaces a control node's measured memory (8Gi), as in AWX. |

### Master key

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AWXNEXT_KMS` | `local` | Master key provider: local (derived from AWXNEXT_SECRET_KEY), vault-transit or azure-keyvault. |
| `AWXNEXT_SECRET_KEY` |  | Local provider: the secret the master key is derived from. Required unless AWXNEXT_DEV is set. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_ADDR` |  | Vault Transit: the server's address. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_KEY` |  | Vault Transit: the key's name (required). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_MOUNT` | `transit` | Vault Transit: the secrets engine's mount. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_NAMESPACE` |  | Vault Transit: the namespace (Vault Enterprise). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_TOKEN` |  | Vault Transit: a token, or AppRole or Kubernetes authentication below. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_ROLE_ID` |  | Vault Transit: AppRole role ID, with AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_SECRET_ID. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_SECRET_ID` |  | Vault Transit: AppRole secret ID. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_K8S_ROLE` |  | Vault Transit: Kubernetes authentication role (the pod's service account token). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_VAULT_CACERT` |  | Vault Transit: CA certificate file of the server. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_VAULT_URL` |  | Azure Key Vault: the vault's URL (required). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_KEY` |  | Azure Key Vault: the key's name (required). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_TENANT_ID` |  | Azure Key Vault: service principal tenant. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_CLIENT_ID` |  | Azure Key Vault: service principal client (or workload identity). |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` |  | Azure Key Vault: service principal secret. |
| `AWXNEXT_KMS_AZURE_MANAGED_IDENTITY` |  | Azure Key Vault: set to use the managed identity. |
| `AWXNEXT_OLD_` |  | Prefix of the previous master key's variables (AWXNEXT_OLD_KMS, AWXNEXT_OLD_SECRET_KEY, ...) for `awxnext keys rewrap`. |

### Images and commands

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AWXNEXT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` |  | Images: the superuser is created before the server starts, its password reset to this on every start. |
| `AWXNEXT_ADMIN_USER` | `admin` | Images: that superuser's name. |
| `AWXNEXT_DB_PASSWORD` |  | Compose: the bundled PostgreSQL's password. |
| `AWXNEXT_DEMO_REPO` |  | Images: where seed-demo creates its playbook repository. |
| `AWXNEXT_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` |  | `awxnext backup` and `restore`: the key escrow's passphrase (or --passphrase-file). |
| `AWXNEXT_PG_DUMP` | pg_dump on the PATH | `awxnext backup`: pg_dump, of the server's major version or newer. |
| `AWXNEXT_PG_RESTORE` | pg_restore on the PATH | `awxnext restore`: pg_restore. |
| `AWX_DATABASE_URL` |  | `awxnext import-awx`: the AWX database (or --source). |
| `AWX_SECRET_KEY` |  | `awxnext import-awx`: AWX's SECRET_KEY, to decrypt its credentials (or --secret-key). |

### Agent

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AWXNEXT_AGENT_URL` |  | Agent: the control plane's URL (or --url). |
| `AWXNEXT_AGENT_TOKEN` |  | Agent: its instance's token (or --token). |
| `AWXNEXT_AGENT_RUNTIME` | `podman` | Agent: podman, docker or none (or --runtime). |
| `AWXNEXT_AGENT_WORK_DIR` | `/var/lib/awxnext-agent` | Agent: job files (or --work-dir). |
| `AWXNEXT_AGENT_CA_CERT` |  | Agent: the CA of the control plane's certificate (or --ca-cert). |
| `AWXNEXT_SHIM_TOKEN` |  | Set by the control plane in container group job pods. |
| `AWXNEXT_SHIM_INSECURE` |  | Container group job pods: skip TLS verification of the control plane (testing). |

### Job event archives

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` |  | Job event archives in Azure Blob Storage without a credential: the account's connection string (else Azure's default chain). For S3 without a credential, AWS's own variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_REGION, ...). |

### Observability

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` |  | OpenTelemetry exporter endpoint; no tracing when neither this nor the next is set. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` |  | OpenTelemetry traces endpoint. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `awxnext` | OpenTelemetry service name. |

## Settings

By category, with the type and default. Settings marked *no effect* are accepted so AWX
clients and imports keep working.

### All (`/api/v2/settings/all/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TOWER_URL_BASE` | string | `""` | Used by services like notifications to render a valid URL to the service. |
| `ACTIVITY_STREAM_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | Record who changed which object, role and setting. Version history is recorded either way. |
| `ACTIVITY_STREAM_ENABLED_FOR_INVENTORY_SYNC` | boolean | `false` | Also record the hosts and groups inventory syncs add and remove. Off by default: a sync can touch thousands of hosts. |
| `ORG_ADMINS_CAN_SEE_ALL_USERS` | boolean | `true` | On: organization admins see every user and team. Off: only those of their organizations. |
| `MANAGE_ORGANIZATION_AUTH` | boolean | `true` | Off: only superusers create, change and delete users and teams and change organization and team roles, for example when an identity provider owns membership. |
| `DEFAULT_EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT` | field | null |  |
| `INSTALL_UUID` | string | `""` |  (read-only, readable by every user) |
| `CUSTOM_VENV_PATHS` | list | `[]` | *No effect.* custom virtual environments are replaced by execution environments. |
| `REMOTE_HOST_HEADERS` | list | `["REMOTE_ADDR","REMOTE_HOST"]` |  |
| `PROXY_IP_ALLOWED_LIST` | list | `[]` |  |
| `SUBSCRIPTIONS_USERNAME` | string | `""` | *No effect.* there are no Red Hat subscriptions to manage. |
| `AUTOMATION_ANALYTICS_GATHER_INTERVAL` | integer | `14400` | *No effect.* nothing is sent to Red Hat analytics. |
| `INSIGHTS_TRACKING_STATE` | boolean | `false` | *No effect.* nothing is sent to Red Hat analytics. |
| `AD_HOC_COMMANDS` | list | `["command","shell","yum","apt","apt_key","apt_repository"...` |  |
| `ALLOW_JINJA_IN_EXTRA_VARS` | choice | `"template"` |  |
| `ALLOW_ANSIBLE_VARS_AT_LAUNCH` | boolean | `false` | Off: launch-time variables, survey questions and answers, schedule and ad hoc variables named ansible_* are refused, as they control how Ansible connects and runs (for example ansible_ssh_common_args). On: AWX's behaviour. Variables on templates, inventories and hosts are not affected. |
| `IGNORE_UNPROMPTED_LAUNCH_FIELDS` | boolean | `false` | Off: a launch that sends a field the template does not prompt for (limit, inventory, extra variables…) is refused. On: AWX's behaviour, the field is ignored, the job starts without it and the response lists it in ignored_fields. |
| `AWX_ISOLATION_BASE_PATH` | string | `"/tmp"` | *No effect.* job directories are under AWXNEXT_JOBS_ROOT. |
| `AWX_ISOLATION_SHOW_PATHS` | list | `[]` | Host paths mounted into execution environment containers, one per entry: HOST-DIR[:CONTAINER-DIR[:OPTIONS]], options such as ro or z. Jobs on the none runtime see the host's files already. |
| `AWX_TASK_ENV` | nested object | `{}` |  |
| `AWX_RUNNER_KEEPALIVE_SECONDS` | integer | `0` | Seconds of silence after which a job's worker sends a keepalive, so quiet tasks on remote execution nodes and container groups are not cut off by idle timeouts. 0: never. |
| `GALAXY_TASK_ENV` | nested object | `{"ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR":"false","GIT_SSH_COMMAND":"ssh -o ...` |  |
| `PROJECT_UPDATE_VVV` | boolean | `false` | *No effect.* project syncs run git directly, not a playbook. |
| `AWX_ROLES_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `AWX_SHOW_PLAYBOOK_LINKS` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `AWX_MOUNT_ISOLATED_PATHS_ON_K8S` | boolean | `false` | Also mount the paths to expose into container group pods, as hostPath volumes of the node the pod runs on. |
| `GALAXY_IGNORE_CERTS` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `STDOUT_MAX_BYTES_DISPLAY` | integer | `1048576` |  |
| `EVENT_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES_DISPLAY` | integer | `1024` | *No effect.* job output shows events in full; MAX_UI_JOB_EVENTS limits how many load at once. |
| `JOB_EVENT_MAX_RATE` | integer | `1000` | Events one job stores per second. Beyond it, consecutive verbose events (plain output lines) are folded into one, so a very verbose job cannot starve the others; its output stays complete. 0: no limit. |
| `MAX_WEBSOCKET_EVENT_RATE` | integer | `30` | Job events sent live to each browser per second; the job page fetches the rest from the API. 0: no limit. |
| `BULK_JOB_MAX_LAUNCH` | integer | `100` |  |
| `BULK_HOST_MAX_CREATE` | integer | `100` |  |
| `BULK_HOST_MAX_DELETE` | integer | `250` |  |
| `SCHEDULE_MAX_JOBS` | integer | `10` | A schedule creates no job while this many jobs of its template are waiting to run. |
| `AWX_ANSIBLE_CALLBACK_PLUGINS` | list | `[]` |  |
| `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_JOB_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_INVENTORY_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_PROJECT_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `ANSIBLE_FACT_CACHE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `MAX_FORKS` | integer | `200` | Most forks a template, launch, schedule, workflow node or ad hoc command may ask for. 0: no limit. |
| `PROJECT_ALLOW_FILE_URLS` | boolean | `false` | Allow git projects to use file:// URLs or local paths on the control plane. Only enable for trusted single-tenant installs. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_HOT_DAYS` | integer | `14` | Days job events stay in the database before they are served from the compressed archive. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_STORAGE` | choice | `"database"` | Where new job event archives are kept. Archives already made stay readable where they are. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_BUCKET` | string | `""` | The S3 bucket or the Azure Blob Storage container of the archives. It must exist. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_PREFIX` | string | `"job-events/"` | Prepended to the archives' keys, followed by the install's INSTALL_UUID, so installs can share a bucket. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_ENDPOINT` | string | `""` | For S3, an S3-compatible service (https://minio.example.com:9000), empty for AWS. For Azure, the account's blob endpoint (https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/). |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_REGION` | string | `""` | The S3 region; empty for the environment's (AWS_REGION), else us-east-1. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_CREDENTIAL` | integer | null | An Amazon Web Services (access key) or Microsoft Azure Resource Manager (client ID and secret) credential. Empty: the environment's (AWS's default chain; AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, or Azure's default chain: environment, workload identity, managed identity). |
| `AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED_ON_PROJECT_SYNC` | boolean | `true` | *No effect.* requirements are installed when a job starts, under AWX_ROLES_ENABLED and AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED. |
| `SESSION_COOKIE_AGE` | integer | `1800` | Seconds without activity after which a session ends (at least 60). |
| `SESSIONS_PER_USER` | integer | `-1` | Logging in beyond this number ends the user's oldest session. -1: no limit. |
| `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH` | boolean | `false` | Disable password login for non-superusers. Superusers keep local login for break-glass access. |
| `AUTH_BASIC_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | Accept a username and password in the Authorization header of API calls. The awx.awx collection uses it unless it is given a token. |
| `OAUTH2_PROVIDER` | nested object | `{"ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_SECONDS":31536000000,"AUTHORIZATION...` | *No effect.* OAuth2 applications are not supported; use personal tokens or OIDC. |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_DIGITS` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of digit characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_UPPER` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of uppercase characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_SPECIAL` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of special characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | AWX's map of the organizations an external user joins, by username or email, applied at each login with the OIDC group mapping: {"Default": {"users": true}, "Ops": {"admins": ["alice@example.com"], "users": "/^[^@]+@example\.com$/i", "remove_users": false}}. Each expression is null (no change), true, false, or strings and /regex/ (flags i, m), matched from the start. An unmatched user is removed unless remove_admins or remove_users is false. A login with its own map (GitHub, Google, Azure AD, SAML) uses that one instead, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | AWX's map of the teams an external user joins, by username or email: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": "/^web-/", "remove": true}}. A login with its own map uses that one instead, as in AWX. |
| `ALLOW_OAUTH2_FOR_EXTERNAL_USERS` | boolean | `false` | *No effect.* OAuth2 applications are not supported; use personal tokens or OIDC. |
| `LOGIN_REDIRECT_OVERRIDE` | string | `""` | Where the web UI sends users who are not logged in, instead of its login page (for example a single sign-on login URL). Open the UI with ?login=local to reach the local login page anyway. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_KEY` | string | `""` | The OIDC key (Client ID) from your IDP. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_SECRET` | string | `""` |  (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_OIDC_ENDPOINT` | string | `""` | The URL for your OIDC provider including the path up to /.well-known/openid-configuration |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_VERIFY_SSL` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `OIDC_SCOPES` | list | `["openid","profile","email","groups"]` |  |
| `OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM` | string | `"preferred_username"` |  |
| `OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` | string | `"groups"` | Claim holding group names. Dotted paths are supported, e.g. realm_access.roles. |
| `OIDC_AUDIENCES` | list | `[]` | Accepted audiences for bearer JWTs. Defaults to the client id. |
| `OIDC_ALLOW_BEARER` | boolean | `true` | Accept access tokens issued by the OIDC provider as API bearer tokens. |
| `OIDC_LINK_EXISTING_USERS` | boolean | `false` | Allow OIDC logins to take over an existing local user with the same username. |
| `OIDC_MAPPING` | list | `[]` | Rules mapping groups to access. Examples: {"group": "awx-admins", "superuser": true}, {"group": "auditors", "auditor": true}, {"group": "ops", "organization": "Ops", "role": "member"}, {"group": "ops-leads", "organization": "Ops", "team": "Leads", "role": "admin"}. Group can be a regex with "group_regex". Mappings are authoritative and re-evaluated on every login. |
| `CUSTOM_LOGIN_INFO` | string | `""` | Text shown on the login page, for example who to ask for an account. (readable by every user) |
| `CUSTOM_LOGO` | string | `""` | Image shown on the login page: a data URL of a GIF, PNG or JPEG image (data:image/png;base64,…). (readable by every user) |
| `MAX_UI_JOB_EVENTS` | integer | `4000` | Events the job output page loads at once; more can be loaded on demand, or the output downloaded. 0: all. (readable by every user) |
| `UI_LIVE_UPDATES_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | Off: the web UI opens no websocket; pages show new data when reloaded. (readable by every user) |
| `PENDO_TRACKING_STATE` | string | `"off"` | *No effect.* the web UI sends no usage data. (readable by every user) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Give this URL as the callback URL of the OAuth application (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_KEY` | string | `""` | The OAuth application's client ID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET` | string | `""` | The OAuth application's client secret. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations users of this login join, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}. Used instead of SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams users of this login join: {"Web": {"organization": "Default", "users": true}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Give this URL as the callback URL of the OAuth application (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_KEY` | string | `""` | The OAuth application's client ID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_SECRET` | string | `""` | The OAuth application's client secret. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_NAME` | string | `""` | The organization users must be members of, as in its URL: https://github.com/<organization>. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations users of this login join, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}. Used instead of SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ORG_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams users of this login join: {"Web": {"organization": "Default", "users": true}}. |

| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TEAM_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams users of this login join: {"Web": {"organization": "Default", "users": true}}. |

| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_HOST` | string | null | Hostname/IP where external logs will be sent to. With HTTPS/HTTP, a URL: https:// is assumed unless http:// is given. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PORT` | integer | null | Port on Logging Aggregator to send logs to (if required and not provided in Logging Aggregator). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TYPE` | choice | null | Format messages for the chosen log aggregator. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_USERNAME` | string | `""` | Username for external log aggregator (if required; HTTP/s only). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PASSWORD` | string | `""` | Password or authentication token for external log aggregator (if required; HTTP/s only). Splunk's HTTP Event Collector token goes here. (secret) |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_LOGGERS` | list | `["awx","activity_stream","job_events","system_tracking","...` | Loggers that send logs to the aggregator: awx (service logs), activity_stream (activity stream records), job_events (job events), system_tracking (facts gathered by jobs), broadcast_websocket (none in awxnext). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_INDIVIDUAL_FACTS` | boolean | `false` | If set, system tracking facts are sent one message per fact, allowing for greater search query granularity. If unset, the facts of a host are sent as a single dictionary. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ENABLED` | boolean | `false` | Enable sending logs to external log aggregator. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TOWER_UUID` | string | `""` | Useful to uniquely identify instances: sent as tower_uuid (INSTALL_UUID when empty). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PROTOCOL` | choice | `"https"` | Protocol used to communicate with log aggregator. HTTPS/HTTP assumes HTTPS unless http:// is explicitly used in the Logging Aggregator hostname. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TCP_TIMEOUT` | integer | `5` | Number of seconds for a TCP connection to external log aggregator to timeout, and between retries. Applies to HTTPS and TCP log aggregator protocols. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_VERIFY_CERT` | boolean | `true` | Flag to control enable/disable of certificate verification when LOG_AGGREGATOR_PROTOCOL is "https". |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_LEVEL` | choice | `"WARNING"` | Level threshold used by log handler. Messages less severe than the threshold are not sent: activity stream, job event and fact messages are INFO, so they need INFO or DEBUG. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_QUEUE_SIZE` | integer | `131072` | How many messages wait for the aggregator. At 90% of it, INFO and DEBUG messages are discarded; when it is full, every new message is. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_MAX_DISK_USAGE_GB` | integer | `1` | *No effect.* there is no rsyslogd, and the queue is kept in memory. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_MAX_DISK_USAGE_PATH` | string | `"/var/lib/awx"` | *No effect.* there is no rsyslogd, and the queue is kept in memory. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_RSYSLOGD_DEBUG` | boolean | `false` | Log each delivery to the aggregator, and its errors, on the server's own log. Useful for debugging connection issues for external log aggregation. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Give this URL as the redirect URI of the application (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_KEY` | string | `""` | The application's client ID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_SECRET` | string | `""` | The application's client secret. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_WHITELISTED_DOMAINS` | list | `[]` | Only users whose email is in one of these domains can log in. Empty allows every domain. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_AUTH_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS` | nested object | `{}` | Extra parameters of the authorization request, such as {"hd": "example.com"} to offer only accounts of a Google Workspace domain. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations users of this login join, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}. Used instead of SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH2_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams users of this login join: {"Web": {"organization": "Default", "users": true}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_AZUREAD_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Give this URL as the redirect URI of the application (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_AZUREAD_OAUTH2_KEY` | string | `""` | The application's client ID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_AZUREAD_OAUTH2_SECRET` | string | `""` | The application's client secret. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_AZUREAD_OAUTH2_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations users of this login join, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}. Used instead of SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_AZUREAD_OAUTH2_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams users of this login join: {"Web": {"organization": "Default", "users": true}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Register awxnext with your identity provider as a service provider with this URL (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_METADATA_URL` | string | `""` | awxnext's service provider metadata, for identity providers that read it. (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID` | string | `""` | The audience of the SAML assertions. Empty uses TOWER_URL_BASE. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_PUBLIC_CERT` | string | `""` | PEM certificate of awxnext as a service provider, published in its metadata. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_PRIVATE_KEY` | string | `""` | PEM private key of the certificate, to sign requests and decrypt assertions. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORG_INFO` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata, by language: {"en-US": {"name": "example", "displayname": "Example", "url": "https://www.example.com"}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TECHNICAL_CONTACT` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata: {"givenName": "Technical Contact", "emailAddress": "techsup@example.com"}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SUPPORT_CONTACT` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata: {"givenName": "Support Contact", "emailAddress": "support@example.com"}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ENABLED_IDPS` | nested object | `{}` | Identity providers by name: {"myidp": {"entity_id": "https://idp.example.com", "url": "https://idp.example.com/sso", "x509cert": "MIIC…", "attr_user_permanent_id": "name_id", "attr_username": "uid", "attr_email": "mail", "attr_first_name": "givenName", "attr_last_name": "sn"}}. The attributes default to the standard OIDs; "name_id" uses the subject's NameID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SECURITY_CONFIG` | nested object | `{"requestedAuthnContext":false}` | python3-saml's security settings. Used: authnRequestsSigned, signatureAlgorithm, wantMessagesSigned, wantAssertionsSigned, wantAssertionsEncrypted, wantNameId, requestedAuthnContext and requestedAuthnContextComparison. A response or its assertion must always be signed. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_EXTRA` | nested object | null | *No effect.* python3-saml's extra service provider settings have no equivalent. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_EXTRA_DATA` | list | null | *No effect.* it keeps no social auth extra data. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations a SAML user joins, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}, as SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, which SAML logins do not use. As in AWX's SAML pipeline, a null expression removes like false. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams a SAML user joins, by username or email: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": true}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORGANIZATION_ATTR` | nested object | null | Organizations from SAML attributes: {"saml_attr": "member-of", "saml_admin_attr": "admin-of", "saml_auditor_attr": "auditor-of", "remove": true, "remove_admins": true, "remove_auditors": true}. With remove (the default), a user loses the memberships SAML gave in organizations the attribute no longer names. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TEAM_ATTR` | nested object | null | Teams from a SAML attribute: {"saml_attr": "team", "remove": true, "team_org_map": [{"team": "Blue", "team_alias": "Blue Team", "organization": "Default"}]}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_USER_FLAGS_BY_ATTR` | nested object | null | Superusers and system auditors from the Role attribute or another attribute: {"is_superuser_role": ["awx_admins"], "is_superuser_attr": "is_superuser", "is_superuser_value": ["IT-Superadmin"], "remove_superusers": true, "is_system_auditor_role": [...], "is_system_auditor_attr": "...", "is_system_auditor_value": [...], "remove_system_auditors": true}. As in AWX, a SAML login without them takes the flags away unless remove_superusers or remove_system_auditors is false. |
| `NAMED_URL_FORMATS` | nested object | `{"credential_types":"<name>+<kind>","credentials":"<name>...` | Read-only list of key-value pairs that shows the standard format of all available named URLs. (read-only) |
| `NAMED_URL_GRAPH_NODES` | nested object | `{"credential_types":{"adj_list":[],"fields":["name","kind...` | Read-only list of key-value pairs that exposes named URL graph topology. Use this list to programmatically generate named URLs for resources (read-only) |

### Authentication (`/api/v2/settings/authentication/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SESSION_COOKIE_AGE` | integer | `1800` | Seconds without activity after which a session ends (at least 60). |
| `SESSIONS_PER_USER` | integer | `-1` | Logging in beyond this number ends the user's oldest session. -1: no limit. |
| `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH` | boolean | `false` | Disable password login for non-superusers. Superusers keep local login for break-glass access. |
| `AUTH_BASIC_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | Accept a username and password in the Authorization header of API calls. The awx.awx collection uses it unless it is given a token. |
| `OAUTH2_PROVIDER` | nested object | `{"ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_SECONDS":31536000000,"AUTHORIZATION...` | *No effect.* OAuth2 applications are not supported; use personal tokens or OIDC. |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_DIGITS` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of digit characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_UPPER` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of uppercase characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `LOCAL_PASSWORD_MIN_SPECIAL` | integer | `0` | Minimum number of special characters required in a local password. 0 means no minimum (readable by every user) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | AWX's map of the organizations an external user joins, by username or email, applied at each login with the OIDC group mapping: {"Default": {"users": true}, "Ops": {"admins": ["alice@example.com"], "users": "/^[^@]+@example\.com$/i", "remove_users": false}}. Each expression is null (no change), true, false, or strings and /regex/ (flags i, m), matched from the start. An unmatched user is removed unless remove_admins or remove_users is false. A login with its own map (GitHub, Google, Azure AD, SAML) uses that one instead, as in AWX. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | AWX's map of the teams an external user joins, by username or email: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": "/^web-/", "remove": true}}. A login with its own map uses that one instead, as in AWX. |
| `ALLOW_OAUTH2_FOR_EXTERNAL_USERS` | boolean | `false` | *No effect.* OAuth2 applications are not supported; use personal tokens or OIDC. |
| `LOGIN_REDIRECT_OVERRIDE` | string | `""` | Where the web UI sends users who are not logged in, instead of its login page (for example a single sign-on login URL). Open the UI with ?login=local to reach the local login page anyway. |

### OIDC (`/api/v2/settings/oidc/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_KEY` | string | `""` | The OIDC key (Client ID) from your IDP. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_SECRET` | string | `""` |  (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_OIDC_ENDPOINT` | string | `""` | The URL for your OIDC provider including the path up to /.well-known/openid-configuration |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_OIDC_VERIFY_SSL` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `OIDC_SCOPES` | list | `["openid","profile","email","groups"]` |  |
| `OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM` | string | `"preferred_username"` |  |
| `OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` | string | `"groups"` | Claim holding group names. Dotted paths are supported, e.g. realm_access.roles. |
| `OIDC_AUDIENCES` | list | `[]` | Accepted audiences for bearer JWTs. Defaults to the client id. |
| `OIDC_ALLOW_BEARER` | boolean | `true` | Accept access tokens issued by the OIDC provider as API bearer tokens. |
| `OIDC_LINK_EXISTING_USERS` | boolean | `false` | Allow OIDC logins to take over an existing local user with the same username. |
| `OIDC_MAPPING` | list | `[]` | Rules mapping groups to access. Examples: {"group": "awx-admins", "superuser": true}, {"group": "auditors", "auditor": true}, {"group": "ops", "organization": "Ops", "role": "member"}, {"group": "ops-leads", "organization": "Ops", "team": "Leads", "role": "admin"}. Group can be a regex with "group_regex". Mappings are authoritative and re-evaluated on every login. |

### LDAP (`/api/v2/settings/ldap/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_LDAP_SERVER_URI` | string | `""` | URI of the LDAP server, such as "ldap://ldap.example.com:389" or "ldaps://ldap.example.com:636". Several servers, separated by spaces or commas, are tried in order. Empty turns this LDAP login off. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN` | string | `""` | DN of the account used for every search. Empty binds anonymously. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD` | string | `""` |  (secret) |
| `AUTH_LDAP_START_TLS` | boolean | `false` | Upgrade ldap:// connections with StartTLS. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_CONNECTION_OPTIONS` | nested object | `{"OPT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT":30,"OPT_REFERRALS":0}` | python-ldap options. Used: OPT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT (seconds), OPT_X_TLS_REQUIRE_CERT (0 does not verify the certificate) and OPT_X_TLS_CACERTFILE; referrals are never followed, others have no effect. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_USER_SEARCH` | list | `[]` | How to find a user: ["OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com", "SCOPE_SUBTREE", "(sAMAccountName=%(user)s)"], or a list of such searches, which must find exactly one user between them. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_USER_DN_TEMPLATE` | string | null | The user's DN, such as "uid=%(user)s,OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com". Used instead of the user search when set. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_USER_ATTR_MAP` | nested object | `{}` | User fields read from LDAP at each login: {"first_name": "givenName", "last_name": "sn", "email": "mail"}. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_SEARCH` | list | `[]` | Where the user's groups are: ["DC=example,DC=com", "SCOPE_SUBTREE", "(objectClass=group)"]. Organization and team maps only see groups this search finds. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_TYPE` | choice | `"MemberDNGroupType"` | How group membership is stored. Nested types follow groups in groups. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_TYPE_PARAMS` | nested object | `{"member_attr":"member","name_attr":"cn"}` | Parameters of the group type, such as member_attr for MemberDNGroupType. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_REQUIRE_GROUP` | string | null | DN of a group users must be in to log in. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_DENY_GROUP` | string | null | DN of a group whose members cannot log in. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_USER_FLAGS_BY_GROUP` | nested object | `{}` | Superusers and system auditors by group, set at each login: {"is_superuser": ["CN=Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com"], "is_system_auditor": "CN=Auditors,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com"}. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | `{}` | Organizations a user joins by group, at each login: {"Ops": {"admins": "CN=Ops Admins,DC=example,DC=com", "auditors": [...], "users": true, "remove_users": false}}. Each of admins, auditors and users is null (no change), true, false, or group DNs; an unmatched user is removed unless remove_admins, remove_auditors or remove_users is false. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | `{}` | Teams a user joins by group: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": "CN=Web,DC=example,DC=com", "remove": true}}. |

| `AUTH_LDAP_5_USER_FLAGS_BY_GROUP` | nested object | `{}` | Superusers and system auditors by group, set at each login: {"is_superuser": ["CN=Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com"], "is_system_auditor": "CN=Auditors,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com"}. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_5_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | `{}` | Organizations a user joins by group, at each login: {"Ops": {"admins": "CN=Ops Admins,DC=example,DC=com", "auditors": [...], "users": true, "remove_users": false}}. Each of admins, auditors and users is null (no change), true, false, or group DNs; an unmatched user is removed unless remove_admins, remove_auditors or remove_users is false. |
| `AUTH_LDAP_5_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | `{}` | Teams a user joins by group: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": "CN=Web,DC=example,DC=com", "remove": true}}. |

### SAML (`/api/v2/settings/saml/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_CALLBACK_URL` | string | `""` | Register awxnext with your identity provider as a service provider with this URL (from TOWER_URL_BASE). (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_METADATA_URL` | string | `""` | awxnext's service provider metadata, for identity providers that read it. (read-only) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID` | string | `""` | The audience of the SAML assertions. Empty uses TOWER_URL_BASE. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_PUBLIC_CERT` | string | `""` | PEM certificate of awxnext as a service provider, published in its metadata. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_PRIVATE_KEY` | string | `""` | PEM private key of the certificate, to sign requests and decrypt assertions. (secret) |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORG_INFO` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata, by language: {"en-US": {"name": "example", "displayname": "Example", "url": "https://www.example.com"}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TECHNICAL_CONTACT` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata: {"givenName": "Technical Contact", "emailAddress": "techsup@example.com"}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SUPPORT_CONTACT` | nested object | `{}` | For the metadata: {"givenName": "Support Contact", "emailAddress": "support@example.com"}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ENABLED_IDPS` | nested object | `{}` | Identity providers by name: {"myidp": {"entity_id": "https://idp.example.com", "url": "https://idp.example.com/sso", "x509cert": "MIIC…", "attr_user_permanent_id": "name_id", "attr_username": "uid", "attr_email": "mail", "attr_first_name": "givenName", "attr_last_name": "sn"}}. The attributes default to the standard OIDs; "name_id" uses the subject's NameID. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SECURITY_CONFIG` | nested object | `{"requestedAuthnContext":false}` | python3-saml's security settings. Used: authnRequestsSigned, signatureAlgorithm, wantMessagesSigned, wantAssertionsSigned, wantAssertionsEncrypted, wantNameId, requestedAuthnContext and requestedAuthnContextComparison. A response or its assertion must always be signed. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_EXTRA` | nested object | null | *No effect.* python3-saml's extra service provider settings have no equivalent. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_EXTRA_DATA` | list | null | *No effect.* it keeps no social auth extra data. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORGANIZATION_MAP` | nested object | null | Organizations a SAML user joins, by username or email: {"Default": {"users": true}}, as SOCIAL_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_MAP, which SAML logins do not use. As in AWX's SAML pipeline, a null expression removes like false. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TEAM_MAP` | nested object | null | Teams a SAML user joins, by username or email: {"Web": {"organization": "Ops", "users": true}}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ORGANIZATION_ATTR` | nested object | null | Organizations from SAML attributes: {"saml_attr": "member-of", "saml_admin_attr": "admin-of", "saml_auditor_attr": "auditor-of", "remove": true, "remove_admins": true, "remove_auditors": true}. With remove (the default), a user loses the memberships SAML gave in organizations the attribute no longer names. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_TEAM_ATTR` | nested object | null | Teams from a SAML attribute: {"saml_attr": "team", "remove": true, "team_org_map": [{"team": "Blue", "team_alias": "Blue Team", "organization": "Default"}]}. |
| `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_USER_FLAGS_BY_ATTR` | nested object | null | Superusers and system auditors from the Role attribute or another attribute: {"is_superuser_role": ["awx_admins"], "is_superuser_attr": "is_superuser", "is_superuser_value": ["IT-Superadmin"], "remove_superusers": true, "is_system_auditor_role": [...], "is_system_auditor_attr": "...", "is_system_auditor_value": [...], "remove_system_auditors": true}. As in AWX, a SAML login without them takes the flags away unless remove_superusers or remove_system_auditors is false. |

### Jobs (`/api/v2/settings/jobs/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AD_HOC_COMMANDS` | list | `["command","shell","yum","apt","apt_key","apt_repository"...` |  |
| `ALLOW_JINJA_IN_EXTRA_VARS` | choice | `"template"` |  |
| `ALLOW_ANSIBLE_VARS_AT_LAUNCH` | boolean | `false` | Off: launch-time variables, survey questions and answers, schedule and ad hoc variables named ansible_* are refused, as they control how Ansible connects and runs (for example ansible_ssh_common_args). On: AWX's behaviour. Variables on templates, inventories and hosts are not affected. |
| `IGNORE_UNPROMPTED_LAUNCH_FIELDS` | boolean | `false` | Off: a launch that sends a field the template does not prompt for (limit, inventory, extra variables…) is refused. On: AWX's behaviour, the field is ignored, the job starts without it and the response lists it in ignored_fields. |
| `AWX_ISOLATION_BASE_PATH` | string | `"/tmp"` | *No effect.* job directories are under AWXNEXT_JOBS_ROOT. |
| `AWX_ISOLATION_SHOW_PATHS` | list | `[]` | Host paths mounted into execution environment containers, one per entry: HOST-DIR[:CONTAINER-DIR[:OPTIONS]], options such as ro or z. Jobs on the none runtime see the host's files already. |
| `AWX_TASK_ENV` | nested object | `{}` |  |
| `AWX_RUNNER_KEEPALIVE_SECONDS` | integer | `0` | Seconds of silence after which a job's worker sends a keepalive, so quiet tasks on remote execution nodes and container groups are not cut off by idle timeouts. 0: never. |
| `GALAXY_TASK_ENV` | nested object | `{"ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR":"false","GIT_SSH_COMMAND":"ssh -o ...` |  |
| `PROJECT_UPDATE_VVV` | boolean | `false` | *No effect.* project syncs run git directly, not a playbook. |
| `AWX_ROLES_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `AWX_SHOW_PLAYBOOK_LINKS` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `AWX_MOUNT_ISOLATED_PATHS_ON_K8S` | boolean | `false` | Also mount the paths to expose into container group pods, as hostPath volumes of the node the pod runs on. |
| `GALAXY_IGNORE_CERTS` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `STDOUT_MAX_BYTES_DISPLAY` | integer | `1048576` |  |
| `EVENT_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES_DISPLAY` | integer | `1024` | *No effect.* job output shows events in full; MAX_UI_JOB_EVENTS limits how many load at once. |
| `JOB_EVENT_MAX_RATE` | integer | `1000` | Events one job stores per second. Beyond it, consecutive verbose events (plain output lines) are folded into one, so a very verbose job cannot starve the others; its output stays complete. 0: no limit. |
| `MAX_WEBSOCKET_EVENT_RATE` | integer | `30` | Job events sent live to each browser per second; the job page fetches the rest from the API. 0: no limit. |
| `BULK_JOB_MAX_LAUNCH` | integer | `100` |  |
| `BULK_HOST_MAX_CREATE` | integer | `100` |  |
| `BULK_HOST_MAX_DELETE` | integer | `250` |  |
| `SCHEDULE_MAX_JOBS` | integer | `10` | A schedule creates no job while this many jobs of its template are waiting to run. |
| `AWX_ANSIBLE_CALLBACK_PLUGINS` | list | `[]` |  |
| `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_JOB_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_INVENTORY_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `DEFAULT_PROJECT_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `ANSIBLE_FACT_CACHE_TIMEOUT` | integer | `0` |  |
| `MAX_FORKS` | integer | `200` | Most forks a template, launch, schedule, workflow node or ad hoc command may ask for. 0: no limit. |
| `PROJECT_ALLOW_FILE_URLS` | boolean | `false` | Allow git projects to use file:// URLs or local paths on the control plane. Only enable for trusted single-tenant installs. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_HOT_DAYS` | integer | `14` | Days job events stay in the database before they are served from the compressed archive. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_STORAGE` | choice | `"database"` | Where new job event archives are kept. Archives already made stay readable where they are. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_BUCKET` | string | `""` | The S3 bucket or the Azure Blob Storage container of the archives. It must exist. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_PREFIX` | string | `"job-events/"` | Prepended to the archives' keys, followed by the install's INSTALL_UUID, so installs can share a bucket. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_ENDPOINT` | string | `""` | For S3, an S3-compatible service (https://minio.example.com:9000), empty for AWS. For Azure, the account's blob endpoint (https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/). |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_REGION` | string | `""` | The S3 region; empty for the environment's (AWS_REGION), else us-east-1. |
| `JOB_EVENTS_ARCHIVE_CREDENTIAL` | integer | null | An Amazon Web Services (access key) or Microsoft Azure Resource Manager (client ID and secret) credential. Empty: the environment's (AWS's default chain; AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, or Azure's default chain: environment, workload identity, managed identity). |
| `AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED_ON_PROJECT_SYNC` | boolean | `true` | *No effect.* requirements are installed when a job starts, under AWX_ROLES_ENABLED and AWX_COLLECTIONS_ENABLED. |

### Logging (`/api/v2/settings/logging/`)

| Setting | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_HOST` | string | null | Hostname/IP where external logs will be sent to. With HTTPS/HTTP, a URL: https:// is assumed unless http:// is given. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PORT` | integer | null | Port on Logging Aggregator to send logs to (if required and not provided in Logging Aggregator). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TYPE` | choice | null | Format messages for the chosen log aggregator. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_USERNAME` | string | `""` | Username for external log aggregator (if required; HTTP/s only). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PASSWORD` | string | `""` | Password or authentication token for external log aggregator (if required; HTTP/s only). Splunk's HTTP Event Collector token goes here. (secret) |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_LOGGERS` | list | `["awx","activity_stream","job_events","system_tracking","...` | Loggers that send logs to the aggregator: awx (service logs), activity_stream (activity stream records), job_events (job events), system_tracking (facts gathered by jobs), broadcast_websocket (none in awxnext). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_INDIVIDUAL_FACTS` | boolean | `false` | If set, system tracking facts are sent one message per fact, allowing for greater search query granularity. If unset, the facts of a host are sent as a single dictionary. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ENABLED` | boolean | `false` | Enable sending logs to external log aggregator. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TOWER_UUID` | string | `""` | Useful to uniquely identify instances: sent as tower_uuid (INSTALL_UUID when empty). |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_PROTOCOL` | choice | `"https"` | Protocol used to communicate with log aggregator. HTTPS/HTTP assumes HTTPS unless http:// is explicitly used in the Logging Aggregator hostname. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_TCP_TIMEOUT` | integer | `5` | Number of seconds for a TCP connection to external log aggregator to timeout, and between retries. Applies to HTTPS and TCP log aggregator protocols. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_VERIFY_CERT` | boolean | `true` | Flag to control enable/disable of certificate verification when LOG_AGGREGATOR_PROTOCOL is "https". |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_LEVEL` | choice | `"WARNING"` | Level threshold used by log handler. Messages less severe than the threshold are not sent: activity stream, job event and fact messages are INFO, so they need INFO or DEBUG. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_QUEUE_SIZE` | integer | `131072` | How many messages wait for the aggregator. At 90% of it, INFO and DEBUG messages are discarded; when it is full, every new message is. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_MAX_DISK_USAGE_GB` | integer | `1` | *No effect.* there is no rsyslogd, and the queue is kept in memory. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_MAX_DISK_USAGE_PATH` | string | `"/var/lib/awx"` | *No effect.* there is no rsyslogd, and the queue is kept in memory. |
| `LOG_AGGREGATOR_RSYSLOGD_DEBUG` | boolean | `false` | Log each delivery to the aggregator, and its errors, on the server's own log. Useful for debugging connection issues for external log aggregation. |
